title: Operation Northwoods: The False Flag Op That Never Was
summary: Josh and Chuck cover Operation Northwoods, a 1962 Joint Chiefs of Staff proposal to stage false flag attacks and pretexts so the US could justify invading Cuba and removing Fidel Castro. They set up the context: Castro's 1959 revolution and Communist Cuba's alliance with the USSR, the Bay of Pigs failure, the Kennedy administration's Operation Mongoose under Bobby Kennedy and General Edward Lansdale, and the ticking clock of possible Soviet missile bases. They describe the wild ideas in the Northwoods memo (staged attacks on Guantanamo, a drone-swapped airliner, a fake MiG attack on a plane, a sunk boatload of Cubans, fake Castro photos, star shells), the memo's signing by Lyman Lemnitzer and its rejection by Kennedy, the attempt to destroy the documents, and how the plan became public through James Bamford's reporting and Oliver Stone's JFK. The episode also includes an opening segment about a movie and a tour, a discussion of false flag operations in general, and a listener mail segment.
topics: Justification for US Military Intervention in Cuba

segments.title: Opening banter and movie plug
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck chat about a niece's movie No Exit, touring with Bonnie Prince Billy and Matt Sweeney, and a Matthew Sweet song. They then tease that the episode is about US planning of false flag operations in the 1960s.

segments.title: What is a false flag operation
segments.summary: They define a false flag operation as staging a fake attack to blame an enemy and justify war, and note the origin in pirates flying friendly flags. They mention Russia's recent accusations against Ukraine and other countries' past uses.

segments.title: Cuba under Castro and US concerns
segments.summary: Castro's 1959 revolution made Cuba the first Communist regime in the Western Hemisphere. Americans worried about its influence in Latin America, US business interests, the Panama Canal, and especially the alliance with the USSR and possible Soviet missile bases.

segments.title: Bay of Pigs and plots against Castro
segments.summary: The failed Bay of Pigs invasion in April 1961 left Kennedy distrustful of his military and intelligence advisors. Senator George Smathers proposed assassinating Castro, and various schemes were discussed behind closed doors. Bobby Kennedy was given responsibility for removing Castro.

segments.title: Operation Mongoose
segments.summary: Operation Mongoose was a plan to destabilize Cuba through sabotage, disorder, and espionage, led by Edward Lansdale with agencies including the CIA and State Department. Its wild ideas included poison cigars and a poisoned scuba suit. The plan was constrained by fear of starting World War Three.

segments.title: Lansdale's ideas and the Joint Chiefs memo
segments.summary: In February 1962 Lansdale proposed ways to topple Castro by October, including star shells to suggest the Second Coming. He sought a justification for military invasion. The Joint Chiefs said the Communist regime was incompatible with Western hemisphere security and argued Cuba was outside the Warsaw Pact. Brigadier General William Craig produced a memo of possible provocations, including Operation Free Ride and Operation Good Times.

segments.title: Operation Northwoods memo and Kennedy's rejection
segments.summary: Chairman Lyman Lemnitzer signed the Justification for US Military Intervention in Cuba memo, which proposed false flag pretexts. Defense Secretary McNamara received it, and Kennedy rejected it outright. Lemnitzer reportedly tried to have documents destroyed.

segments.title: Specific Northwoods false flag proposals
segments.summary: The memo's proposals included staged attacks on Guantanamo Bay, over-the-fence attacks, a hijacked-looking charter flight swapped for a drone, a fake MiG attack on a US plane, a sunk boat of Cubans, and fake attacks on Cuban exiles in Miami. Ideas were designed to make the attacks seem unrelated. Hosts note that most plans avoided actual deaths but some could have escalated.

segments.title: Aftermath, cover-up, and disclosure
segments.summary: After Kennedy rejected the plan, Operation Mongoose was shut down and Cottrell replaced Lansdale. Plans continued in the Joint Chiefs for a while. Castro outlived the planners. Investigative journalist James Bamford called it among the most corrupt plans ever created, and Oliver Stone's JFK movie helped bring the documents to light.

segments.title: Listener mail from a night shift nurse
segments.summary: Listener Lindsay Johnson writes about her husband picking episodes at random and how she listens on her commute. Hosts discuss listening orders, the sandwiching idea, and thank her.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck close the episode and give the show's contact address and credits.
